title: fix(fused_mlp): drop extra -8*scales on gemm zero-point arg
body:
#### What does this implement/fix?

`QuantLlamaMLP.our_llama_mlp` passes `scaled_zeros - 8 * scales` to `gemm_forward_cuda_new` on the prefill path (`x.numel() // x.shape[-1] >= 8`), but the gemv path and `WQLinear.forward` both pass `scaled_zeros` unchanged.

The AWQ gemm kernel dequantizes as `raw * scale + zero`, where `scaled_zeros` is already `-zero_point * scale`. Subtracting another `8 * scales` shifts every weight by `-8 * scale` per channel, so prefill MLP outputs are systematically wrong.

#### Root cause

Leftover from an old unsigned int4 mapping; `WQLinear` removed this shift (see comment in `qmodule.py`) but `fused_mlp.py` gemm calls did not.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: fix(llama): use LlamaConfig for LlamaRotaryEmbedding on transformers 4.48+
body:
## Summary

Fixes TinyChat initialization failure on transformers 4.48+ caused by a breaking change in `LlamaRotaryEmbedding`.

In transformers 4.48, `LlamaRotaryEmbedding` no longer accepts `head_dim` and `max_position_embeddings` as direct keyword arguments. Instead, it expects a `LlamaConfig` object. TinyChat's `LlamaAttentionFused` was still using the old API, which raised an error during model init.

This PR constructs a minimal `LlamaConfig` with the required fields and passes it to `LlamaRotaryEmbedding`, restoring compatibility with transformers 4.48+.

Fixes #269

## Test plan

- [ ] Install transformers >= 4.48
- [ ] Run TinyChat Llama demo / load a Llama AWQ model without init errors
- [ ] Confirm `LlamaAttentionFused` initializes and rotary embeddings work as before
- [ ] Verify behavior on transformers < 4.48 if applicable

title: feat(rocm): add AMD ROCm/HIP support for AWQ inference engine on MI300X/MI325X
body:
## Summary

This PR adds AMD ROCm/HIP support for the AWQ inference engine, enabling INT4 GEMV/GEMM quantized LLM inference on AMD Instinct GPUs.

Closes #194

## Tested configuration

- **GPU:** AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942)  
- **ROCm:** 7.2.4  
- **PyTorch:** 2.12.1+rocm7.1  

## Verification

All 14 ops load successfully and INT4 GEMV correctness is confirmed:

```
IMPORT OK
Ops: ['fused_rope_with_pos_forward_func', 'gelu_and_quant', 'gemm_forward_cuda',
      'gemm_forward_cuda_new', 'gemv_forward_cuda', 'gemv_forward_cuda_new',
      'invoke_quant', 'layernorm_forward_cuda', 'rms_norm_general',
      'rotary_embedding_neox', 'silu_and_mul', 'single_query_attention',
      'w8a8_gemm_forward_cuda', 'w8a8_gemm_fuse_bias_forward_cuda']
GEMV OK: shape=[1, 4096], dtype=float16, norm=12976.0
```

### INT4 GEMV throughput on MI300X

| Shape (m × n × k) | Latency | TFLOPS |
|---|---|---|
| 1 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.005 ms | 7.08 |
| 1 × 4096 × 11008 | 0.010 ms | 8.98 |
| 1 × 8192 × 8192 | 0.016 ms | 8.23 |

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `awq/kernels/setup.py` | Auto-detect ROCm build; add HIP compile flags and hipblas linkage |
| `awq/kernels/csrc/hip_compat.h` | CUDA→HIP type aliases (bfloat16, shfl_sync, WARP_SIZE=64) |
| `awq/kernels/hipsparse_stub/` | Minimal stub headers for ROCm build compatibility |
| `awq/kernels/csrc/quantization_new/gemv/gemv_cuda.cu` | Fix WARP_SIZE=64 for AMD CDNA wavefronts |
| `awq/kernels/csrc/quantization_new/gemm/gemm_cuda.cu/.h` | Fix function signatures for ROCm symbol resolution |
| `awq/kernels/csrc/w8a8/w8a8_gemm_cuda.cu` | AMD stub for W8A8 fused ops |
| `awq/kernels/csrc/attention/decoder_masked_multihead_attention.cu` | Lightweight AMD stub |
| `ROCM.md` | Build instructions and benchmark results |

## Key porting notes

- PyTorch hipify translates CUDA→HIP automatically at build time — `nv_bfloat162` aliases in source map correctly through hipify
- `WARP_SIZE` must be 64 on AMD CDNA (wavefront width); original had a hardcoded override causing wrong shared-mem sizing
- Build requires `torch+rocm7.x` matching the container ROCm version

Full AMD-maintained reference repo: https://github.com/AMD-AIOSS/ROCm-LLM-AWQ

title: Move rotary_emb to target device for LlavaLlamaForCausalLM to avoid device mismatch
body:
Bug:
When performing AWQ search and quantization on `LlavaLlamaForCausalLM` models, a `RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but found at least two devices, cpu and cuda:0!` is raised during the model execution/forward flow.

Root Cause:
In `awq/quantize/pre_quant.py`, the `move_embed` function handles moving embed weights and rotary embeddings for standard LLaMA and Qwen models, but for `LlavaLlamaForCausalLM` it only moves `model.model.embed_tokens` and vision tower embeddings, leaving the rotary embeddings `model.model.rotary_emb` on the CPU (leading to device mismatches during forward execution on GPU).

Why Fix is Correct:
By explicitly moving `model.model.rotary_emb` to the target `device` in the `LlavaLlamaForCausalLM` condition within `move_embed`, we guarantee that all relevant LLM/Llava model components reside on the same GPU device during the quantization process.

title: fix(fused_mlp): drop extra '-8 * scales' shift on gemm path
body:
### Bug

In ` QuantLlamaMLP.our_llama_mlp ` (` tinychat/modules/fused_mlp.py `), the gemm path passes ` scaled_zeros - 8 * scales ` as the zero-point argument to ` gemm_forward_cuda_new `:

```python
gate_output = awq_inference_engine.gemm_forward_cuda_new(
    x,
    self.gate_proj_qweight,
    self.gate_proj_scales,
    self.gate_proj_scaled_zeros - 8 * self.gate_proj_scales,
)
```

This is inconsistent with both:

- The gemv path a few lines above, which passes ` self.gate_proj_scaled_zeros ` unmodified.
- ` WQLinear.forward ` in ` awq/quantize/qmodule.py ` (the canonical quantized linear), whose gemm call is ` gemm_forward_cuda_new(inputs, qweight, scales, scaled_zeros) ` — the trailing ` # - 8.0 * self.scales) ` comment is a leftover noting that this shift was removed.

### Root cause

` dequantize_s4_to_fp16x2 ` in ` awq/kernels/csrc/quantization_new/dequantize.cuh ` keeps the int4 weights *unsigned* in ` [0, 15] ` (see the explicit comment "Haotian: subtract {1024, 1024} instead, we do not need to map to [-8, 7]" / ` FP16_TOP_MAGIC_NUM = 0x6400 `). The gemm kernel in ` awq/kernels/csrc/quantization_new/gemm/gemm_cuda.cu ` then applies ` __hfma2(loaded, scale, zero) ` — i.e., ` raw * scale + zero `.

For this to recover the original ` (raw - zero_point) * scale `, the kernel needs ` zero == -zero_point * scale `. That is exactly what ` WQLinear.from_linear ` builds into ` scaled_zeros ` (` scaled_zeros[:, :scales.shape[1]] = -(qscales * zeros) `).

Subtracting another ` 8 * scales ` here therefore biases every dequantized weight by an extra ` -8 * scale `, so each fused MLP output is off by ` -8 * scale_sum_over_K ` per output channel whenever the gemm branch fires (` x.numel() / x.shape[-1] >= 8 `, e.g. prefill).

### Fix

Pass ` scaled_zeros ` directly, matching both the gemv branch and ` WQLinear.forward `:

```python
self.gate_proj_scaled_zeros,
...
self.up_proj_scaled_zeros,
```

The gemv path (` numel/last_dim < 8 `) already uses these tensors as-is, so behavior on small batches is unchanged; only the previously-broken gemm path on larger batches is corrected.

title: fix: use c_fc.out_features for BigCode ScaledActivation scale dimension
body:
## Bug

In `scale_activations` (`awq/quantize/quantizer.py`), the BigCode branch initializes the `ScaledActivation` scale vector using `module.mlp.c_proj.out_features`:

```python
elif "bigcode" in str(module.__class__).lower():
    ...
    c = module.mlp.c_proj.out_features   # wrong
    act = ScaledActivation(
        module.mlp.act, torch.ones(c, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    )
```

## Root cause

`module.mlp.act` (the GeLU activation) sits **between** `c_fc` and `c_proj` in the BigCode MLP stack:

```
x → c_fc (hidden → 4h) → act → c_proj (4h → hidden) → output
```

The `ScaledActivation` scale must match the output dimension of the layer that feeds *into* the activation, which is `c_fc.out_features` (the intermediate/4h size). Using `c_proj.out_features` (the smaller hidden dimension) creates a scale vector of the wrong size.

Every other architecture in the same function uses the first linear layer's output dimension:

| Architecture | Code |
|---|---|
| Bloom | `dense_h_to_4h.out_features` |
| Falcon | `dense_h_to_4h.out_features` |
| NeoX | `dense_h_to_4h.out_features` |
| MPT | `ffn.up_proj.out_features` |
| **BigCode** | `c_proj.out_features` ← **wrong** |

## Fix

Change `c_proj.out_features` to `c_fc.out_features`, matching the pattern used by all other architectures.

title: Fix KeyError writing output_path when --tasks=wikitext
body:
## Bug

`awq/entry.py` crashes with `KeyError: 'config'` when run with
`--tasks wikitext --output_path <file>`.

## Root cause

The wikitext branch builds `results = {\"ppl\": ppl.item()}` and writes it
inside a nested `if args.output_path is not None:` block. After the
if/else for task type finishes, a second `if args.output_path is not
None:` block runs unconditionally and does:

```python
results[\"config\"][\"model\"] = args.model_path
with open(args.output_path, \"w\") as f:
    json.dump(results, f, indent=2)
```

But the wikitext `results` dict has no `\"config\"` key — only lm-eval's
`simple_evaluate()` return value has that structure. So the wikitext
path always hits `KeyError: 'config'` before it can write its output
file again, and any earlier correct write from lines 330-333 is
followed immediately by a crash.

## Why the fix is correct

Indenting the second output-path block into the `else` branch
limits the `results[\"config\"][\"model\"] = ...` statement to the path
where `results` actually has a `config` dict (from
`lm_eval.evaluator.simple_evaluate`). The wikitext branch keeps its
existing correct `json.dump(results, ...)` block. No behavioural
change for the non-wikitext path.

## Change

`awq/entry.py`: indent the trailing `if args.output_path is not None:`
block inside the lm-eval `else` arm. One-block (6 lines) indentation
change, no logic changes.

title: Guard ln.bias.div_ in smooth_ln_fcs for LayerNorm(bias=False)
body:
## Bug

`awq/quantize/smooth.py::smooth_ln_fcs` unconditionally scales `ln.bias`:

```python
    ln.weight.div_(scales)
    ln.bias.div_(scales)
```

`nn.LayerNorm` accepts `bias=False` (PyTorch 2.1+), in which case the module has no `bias` parameter and `ln.bias is None`. Calling `.div_()` on `None` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'div_'`, killing smoothing for any model that uses bias-free LayerNorm (certain VLM and efficient-LLM variants).

## Root cause

The sibling rescaler `auto_scale.scale_ln_fcs`, which mirrors the same smoothing identity, already guards this case:

```python
ln.weight.div_(scales)
if hasattr(ln, "bias") and ln.bias is not None:
    ln.bias.div_(scales)
```

`smooth.py` just wasn't updated when the guard was added to `auto_scale.py`.

## Why the fix is correct

Adopt the exact same guard here:

```diff
     ln.weight.div_(scales)
-    ln.bias.div_(scales)
+    if hasattr(ln, "bias") and ln.bias is not None:
+        ln.bias.div_(scales)
```

- Models with a real `ln.bias` (the common case): guard evaluates `True`, behaviour unchanged — `ln.bias.div_(scales)` still runs.
- Models with `ln.bias=None` (LayerNorm(bias=False)): guard evaluates `False`, skipping the crash. This matches the smoothing identity, which has no bias term to rescale when the norm has no bias.
- The `hasattr` branch of the predicate is what `auto_scale.py` uses; keeping the same shape makes the two call sites easy to keep in sync in future.

Two added lines, one removed — net +1. No other changes to `smooth_ln_fcs` or the file.

title: Fix pseudo_quantize_tensor NameError on zero_point=False branch
body:
### Bug
`pseudo_quantize_tensor` raises `NameError` in the `zero_point=False` branch because the first line asserts on a name that is never bound in that branch:

https://github.com/mit-han-lab/llm-awq/blob/d6e797a/awq/quantize/quantizer.py#L69-L83

```python
if zero_point:
    max_val = w.amax(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    min_val = w.amin(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    ...
else:  # we actually never used this
    assert min_val is None
    max_val = w.abs().amax(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    ...
```

`min_val` is only bound inside the `zero_point=True` branch, so in the `else` branch Python raises `NameError: name 'min_val' is not defined` before the assert can even be evaluated. Any caller that reaches this path (e.g. passing a `q_config` with `zero_point=False` through `auto_clip_layer` / `_search_module_scale`) crashes instead of taking the symmetric-quantization path that follows.

### Root cause
An orphaned sanity-check assert left over from an earlier version of the function where `min_val` was in scope. It now references an undefined name.

### Fix
Drop the assert. The rest of the `else` branch already recomputes `max_val`/`scales` from scratch and does not rely on `min_val`, so removing the line restores the intended symmetric-quantization path without changing behaviour for the `zero_point=True` case.

title: Fix move_embed NameError when tinychat is not installed
body:
## Bug

`move_embed()` in `awq/quantize/pre_quant.py` calls `isinstance(model, LlavaLlamaForCausalLM)` at line 69. Since #294 made `from tinychat.models import LlavaLlamaForCausalLM` optional:

```python
try:
    from tinychat.models import LlavaLlamaForCausalLM
except ImportError as e:
    pass
```

When `tinychat` is not installed, the symbol is never bound. Any model that doesn't match the earlier `LlamaForCausalLM`/`Qwen2ForCausalLM`/`InternVL3` branches (i.e., `OPT`, `BLOOM`, `MPT`, `Falcon`, `BigCode`, `GPT-NeoX`, `LlavaLlamaModel`) falls through to line 69 and raises `NameError: name 'LlavaLlamaForCausalLM' is not defined` — breaking `run_awq` for every AWQ-supported non-Llama model on a tinychat-less install.

## Root cause

#294 deliberately made the tinychat import optional but missed this one `isinstance` call. `get_blocks()` already uses string-based matching for the same class (line 35: `model.__class__.__name__ == \"LlavaLlamaForCausalLM\"`), as does the `InternVL3` branch in the same function (line 61) and the `LlavaLlamaModel` branch (line 95).

## Fix

Switch line 69 to the same `__class__.__name__` comparison. This preserves the original behavior when `tinychat` is installed (a `LlavaLlamaForCausalLM` instance still matches by class name) and no longer references the unbound symbol when it isn't.

title: Fix Qwen2 decode path passing raw rope_scaling factor instead of 1/factor
body:
## Bug

\`Qwen2AttentionFused.__init__\` resolves \`config.rope_scaling\` to a scalar that is later passed to the awq_inference_engine kernel during decode:

\`\`\`python
self.rope_scaling = config.rope_scaling
if self.rope_scaling is None:
    self.rope_scaling = 1.0
elif isinstance(self.rope_scaling, dict):
    self.rope_scaling = self.rope_scaling.get(\"factor\", 1.0)
\`\`\`

For e.g. \`{\"type\": \"linear\", \"factor\": 4.0}\` it stores \`4.0\` and then calls

\`\`\`python
awq_inference_engine.single_query_attention(
    ..., self.rope_theta, self.rope_scaling, True,
)
\`\`\`

## Root cause

The prefill path in the same file (\`Transformer.__init__\`, lines 343-347) precomputes the rotary frequencies with \`1.0 / rope_scale[\"factor\"]\`, and the sibling tinychat models do the same:

- \`tinychat/models/llama.py:104\` — \`self.rope_scaling = 1.0 / self.rope_scaling[\"factor\"]\`
- \`tinychat/models/falcon.py:132\` — \`self.rope_scaling = 1.0 / self.rope_scaling[\"factor\"]\`

Only Qwen2 stores the raw factor, so the decode-time per-token rotary uses a different scale than the precomputed prefill freqs. The two paths disagree, silently shifting positions during long-context generation on Qwen2 models that actually configure rope scaling.

## Fix

Apply the same \`1.0 /\` so the decode-time scalar matches the prefill convention and the LLaMA / Falcon implementations.

title: Fix scale_fc_fc dividing full bias when only last N rows of weight are scaled
body:
## Bug

In \`awq/quantize/auto_scale.py\`, \`scale_fc_fc\` scales only the last \`scales.size(0)\` rows of \`fc1.weight\` but divides the **entire** bias vector:

\`\`\`python
fc1.weight[-scales.size(0) :].div_(scales.view(-1, 1))
if fc1.bias is not None:
    fc1.bias.div_(scales.view(-1))
\`\`\`

## Root cause

The \`[-scales.size(0):]\` slice on the weight is deliberate: for fused projections where \`fc1.out_features > scales.size(0)\` and only the trailing slice of \`fc1\`'s output actually feeds into \`fc2\`, the smoothing transform should touch only those rows. The canonical case is BLOOM's \`self_attention.query_key_value\`, a fused \`[q | k | v]\` projection where the caller (\`_auto_get_scale(prev_op=module.self_attention.query_key_value, layers=[module.self_attention.dense], ...)\`) supplies scales sized to the v slice so that v→dense is smoothed.

The bias, however, is divided across all \`3*H\` components. For BLOOM (which has \`bias=True\` on the fused qkv), this scales the q and k bias entries by a factor that was only meant to compensate v's weight change; downstream q/k outputs get corrupted.

## Fix

Apply the same trailing slice to the bias:

\`\`\`python
fc1.bias[-scales.size(0) :].div_(scales.view(-1))
\`\`\`

## Why this is safe

When \`scales.size(0) == fc1.out_features\` (no-fused-projection case), \`fc1.bias[-scales.size(0):]\` covers the entire bias, so the fix matches the existing behavior. The only changed path is the partial-slice case, which previously mis-scaled bias entries that do not feed \`fc2\`.

title: Fix BigCode ScaledActivation using down-projection dimension
body:
## Bug

In `scale_activations()`, the BigCode branch creates a `ScaledActivation` with `c = module.mlp.c_proj.out_features`. `c_proj` is the down-projection (inner_dim → hidden_size), but the activation sits between `c_fc` (up-projection) and `c_proj`, so its dimension should be `c_fc.out_features` (= inner_dim).

Every other architecture correctly uses the up-projection's `out_features`:
- Bloom: `dense_h_to_4h.out_features`
- MPT: `up_proj.out_features`
- Falcon: `dense_h_to_4h.out_features`
- NeoX: `dense_h_to_4h.out_features`

## Root cause

`c_proj` was used instead of `c_fc` — likely a typo since both are attributes of `module.mlp`.

## Fix

`c_proj.out_features` → `c_fc.out_features`

title: Fix auto_clip_layer excluding max_shrink boundary from grid search
body:
## Summary

`auto_clip_layer` grid-searches for the optimal weight-clipping threshold by shrinking `org_max_val` in `n_grid` steps down to `max_shrink`. The loop uses `range(int(max_shrink * n_grid))`, which is exclusive — so the clipping level at exactly `max_shrink` is never evaluated.

With defaults `max_shrink=0.5` and `n_grid=20`:
- `range(int(0.5 * 20))` = `range(10)` → `i_s` ∈ {0, ..., 9}
- Tightest clip tested: `org_max_val * (1 - 9/20)` = **0.55x**
- `max_shrink` boundary (0.50x) is skipped

This means the most aggressive clipping level is never tried, potentially leaving quantization accuracy on the table.

**Fix**: `range(int(max_shrink * n_grid) + 1)` to include the boundary.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified the off-by-one with default parameters in Python REPL
- [ ] Existing quantization tests should continue to pass

title: Fix Falcon prefill RotaryEmbedding ignoring config.rope_theta
body:
## Bug

`FalconAttentionFused.__init__` in \`tinychat/models/falcon.py\` constructs its prefill `RotaryEmbedding` with the default `base=10000`, ignoring the configured `rope_theta`. The decode path of the same class uses `self.rope_theta` when calling the fused kernel, so prefill and decode end up applying different rotary base frequencies for any Falcon variant whose \`config.rope_theta\` isn't 10000.

## Root cause

\`\`\`python
# __init__
self.rotary_emb = RotaryEmbedding(self.head_dim)      # <-- base defaults to 10000
self.rope_theta = args.rope_theta
self.rope_scaling = args.rope_scaling
...

# forward, prefill (seqlen > 1)
xq, xk = self.rotary_emb(xq, xk)                      # uses the default 10000 base

# forward, decode (seqlen == 1)
output = awq_inference_engine.single_query_attention(
    xq, xk, xv, self.cache_k, self.cache_v,
    None, None,
    start_pos, self.head_dim,
    self.rope_theta, self.rope_scaling, True,          # uses args.rope_theta
)
\`\`\`

`RotaryEmbedding.__init__` computes `inv_freq = 1.0 / (base ** (torch.arange(0, head_dim, 2).float() / head_dim))`, so the `base` parameter directly controls the rotary frequencies baked into `cos_cached`/`sin_cached`. With the prefill hard-coded to 10000, q/k are rotated with one set of frequencies during the context stage, and then with a different set for every subsequent decode step — silently corrupting attention as soon as generation transitions past the prompt.

The same class already reads `args.rope_theta` and threads it through the decode path, confirming that the intent was for the layer to use the configured value end-to-end.

## Fix

Pass `base=self.rope_theta` to `RotaryEmbedding` at construction time so both prefill and decode share the same rotary base:

\`\`\`diff
-        self.rotary_emb = RotaryEmbedding(self.head_dim)
         self.rope_theta = args.rope_theta
         self.rope_scaling = args.rope_scaling
+        self.rotary_emb = RotaryEmbedding(self.head_dim, base=self.rope_theta)
\`\`\`

For the common case `rope_theta == 10000` behavior is unchanged (the default already matched the hard-coded value), so this is a pure correctness fix for non-default Falcon configurations.

## Notes

- Not touching `rope_scaling`: the prefill `RotaryEmbedding` doesn't currently implement scaling at all, and wiring it up is a larger change than the scope of this PR. This PR keeps the change strictly to restoring parity on `rope_theta`.

title: Stop mutating caller's stop_token_ids list in stream generators
body:
### Bug

All four stream generators under `tinychat/stream_generators/` (`StreamGenerator`, `LlavaStreamGenerator`, `InternVLStreamGenerator`, `NVILAStreamGenerator`) do the same thing just before their generation loop:

\`\`\`python
stop_token_ids.append(tokenizer.eos_token_id)
\`\`\`

and declare the parameter as \`stop_token_ids=[]\`.

### Root cause

Every real caller (e.g. \`tinychat/demo.py\`, \`tinychat/vila10_demo.py\`, \`tinychat/vila15_demo.py\`, \`tinychat/internvl_demo.py\`, \`tinychat/nvila_demo.py\`, \`tinychat/serve/model_worker*.py\`) builds \`stop_token_ids\` once from \`get_stop_token_ids(...)\` and passes the same list on every turn of a \`while True\` chat loop:

\`\`\`python
stop_token_ids = get_stop_token_ids(args.model_type, args.model_path)
...
while True:
    ...
    output_stream = stream_generator(
        ...,
        stop_token_ids=stop_token_ids,
        ...,
    )
\`\`\`

Because the generator mutates the passed list in place, every turn appends another copy of the eos id to the caller's list and it grows unboundedly over the session. The \`stop_token_ids=[]\` default is the usual mutable-default trap on top of that: callers that omit the argument accumulate eos ids in a shared default across invocations.

\`in\`-checks still work, so generation doesn't visibly break, but callers' lists keep growing and the defaults get polluted across calls — clearly not what the code intends.

### Fix

Rebind \`stop_token_ids\` to a fresh local list that includes eos, instead of mutating the argument:

\`\`\`python
stop_token_ids = list(stop_token_ids) + [tokenizer.eos_token_id]
\`\`\`

This keeps the rest of the function (the \`if token in stop_token_ids\` stop check) working exactly as before without touching the caller's list or the shared default. Applied to all four generators, one line each (4 lines total).

title: Fix NameError in pseudo_quantize_tensor when zero_point=False
body:
## Summary

`pseudo_quantize_tensor()` in `awq/quantize/quantizer.py` crashes with `NameError` when called with `zero_point=False`.

**Root cause:** `min_val` is only assigned inside the `if zero_point:` branch (line 71). The `else` branch (symmetric quantization) has `assert min_val is None` on line 77, but since `min_val` was never defined in this scope, Python raises `NameError` before the assertion can even evaluate.

**Fix:** Remove the vestigial assertion. `min_val` is not used anywhere in the symmetric quantization path — the code correctly computes `max_val` from `w.abs().amax()` and derives scales from that alone.

The comment `# we actually never used this` on the `else` branch confirms this path was written speculatively and the assertion was never tested at runtime.

## Test plan

- [ ] Call `pseudo_quantize_tensor(w, zero_point=False)` — previously crashes, now runs correctly
- [ ] Verify `pseudo_quantize_tensor(w, zero_point=True)` behavior is unchanged

title: Fix hardcoded filter threshold in calibration data loading
body:
## Summary

- Fix bug in `awq/utils/calib_data.py` where the sample length filter in `get_calib_dataset` uses a hardcoded value of `512` instead of the `block_size` parameter
- This bug is latent at the default `block_size=512` but manifests when users pass a non-default value (e.g. `block_size=2048` for long-context models), causing samples longer than 512 tokens to be incorrectly skipped even though they fit within the requested block size

## Test plan

- Verified the fix is a single-line change from `if len(line_encoded) > 512:` to `if len(line_encoded) > block_size:`
- At the default `block_size=512`, behavior is unchanged
- With `block_size=2048`, samples between 513 and 2048 tokens are now correctly included instead of being filtered out

title: Fix position_ids shape mismatch for Llama3 on newer transformers
body:
## Summary
- Fixes a `RuntimeError` when running AWQ quantization on Llama3 models with transformers >= 4.56
- The `Catcher` class captures `position_ids` during calibration, but the captured shape may not match the input sequence length in subsequent layer forward passes
- Regenerates `position_ids` from the actual input sequence length (`torch.arange(seq_len).unsqueeze(0)`) before each layer call to ensure consistent shapes

## Root Cause
In newer transformers versions, `apply_rotary_pos_emb` expects `position_ids` (and derived `cos`/`sin` tensors) to have the same sequence dimension as the query/key states. The `position_ids` captured once by the `Catcher` at layer 0 can have a mismatched shape when reused across layers, causing:
```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (32) must match the size of tensor b (128) at non-singleton dimension 3
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Run AWQ quantization on Llama3-8B with transformers >= 4.56 and confirm no shape mismatch error
- [ ] Verify quantization results remain correct (scales and clips unchanged)
- [ ] Test with older transformers versions to confirm backward compatibility

Fixes #303
